answer: Proof-of-Space-Time resists Sybil attacks by requiring each agent to seal an identity-bound dataset and answer random sector challenges within a tight latency delta. Because re-encoding takes longer than that window, attackers cannot recompute proofs on demand and must fund dedicated disk capacity and IOPS per clone rather than hoarding keys in a cold glacier. Networks can raise storage quotas at each trust terrace, though well-funded adversaries can still rent bulk cloud disks.
